note: The document reader's declared settings (#280, #281 gaps 1, 12 and 13; scripts/text_extract.py, scripts/pdf_layers.py, scripts/html_layers.py). `replacement_character_share_above`: a text or HTML file is read as UTF-8 with every invalid byte replaced by U+FFFD; when the replaced characters are more than this share of the text read, the reader warns and records the encoding layer as lost. Not measured against any corpus: one replaced character in a thousand is the operator's starting value. `html_track_changes` names the markup the HTML reader takes as an insertion or a deletion (elements, class tokens) and the attributes it reads an author and a date from, first match wins.
pdf_layout_note: D-668: how a PDF's layout is read from where its text is drawn (scripts/pdf_layout.py, scripts/pdf_layers.py). Sizes are in em (the text's own size), shares of the page or of a column. line_tolerance_em: pieces this close in height are one line. cell_gap_em: a wider gap on a line starts a new cell. margin_band_share: the top and bottom share of a page a running header or footer stands in; repeat_pages_min: on how many pages its text (digits read as one mark) must repeat. column_lines_min: how many lines must split at a gutter; column_fill_share: how much of its column a left cell must fill (a table's short cells do not). align_tolerance_em and table_rows_min: cells starting this close, on this many lines, are a table. heading_size_ratio and heading_chars_max: a one-line block this much larger than the body size and at most this long is a heading. line_fill_share: a line filling this share of its column runs on into the next. char_width_em: a character's estimated width, since the text visitor hands no glyph widths. Not measured against any corpus: the operator's starting values, proven on the gate's built PDFs. With the block missing or any value not a positive number, no layout is recovered and the record says so.
